messages.author: 6d3f7222550fe21b
messages.subject: cast reshape long to wide
parts:
Is "cast" a good variable for turning a long-form dataset into wide? Can it compete with "reshape", and if so, how?

All the examples in the "cast" help file appear to be about transforming or summarizing the data, not just reshaping.

In the example below, I turn a wide dataframe into a long dataframe using melt. To recover the wide dataframe, I use reshape and gsub. Can it be done more simply using cast?

Example:

set.seed(1)
junkwide<-data.frame( id=LETTERS[1:5], age=6:10
, t1=round(3*rnorm(5))
, t2=round(4*rnorm(5))
, t3=round(5*rnorm(5))
)
junkwide[4,4]<-NA
junkwide
junklong <- melt(junkwide, id.vars=c("id", "age"))
junklong
# Using reshape:
recoveredwide<- reshape(junklong, direction="wide", idvar=c("id", "age"), timevar="variable")
recoveredwide
names( recoveredwide) <-gsub( "value.", "", names( recoveredwide) )
recoveredwide

# Can "cast" do better? How?

messages.author: a5be32bcb3d808db
messages.subject: Re: cast reshape long to wide
parts:
Hi Jacob,
You can get back to your wide form just by using

cast(junklong)

But that is kind of cheating, because melt stores information about
the original state that cast then uses by default. If you had started
with junklong, you could convert it to the wide form using

cast(junklong, ... ~ variable)

Best,
Ista
